learningGoals: Identify and name familiar places, people, and things seen in the neighborhood. 🏘️
Understand simple directional and sequence words related to a journey. ➡️
Describe daily morning routines and the commute to school. 🎒
Enhance observation skills by discussing the environment outside the home. 🌳
Read short narrative sentences that describe a sequence of events. 📖
conversationStarters: Can you remember three interesting things we pass by when we travel from our home to your school? 🧐
Who are the people you see every morning on your way to school? 👨‍🍳
If you could add anything fun to our route to school, like a slide or a zoo, what would it be? 🎢
teachingTips: Draw a simple map together showing your home, the road, a few landmarks, and the school to build spatial awareness. 🗺️
Use sequence words like 'First, we leave home. Next, we walk on the road. Then, we reach school.' to teach order. 🔢
Point out signboards and shop names during your actual commute and try to read the simple English words together. 🪧
Relate the story in the chapter to their personal daily routine to make the reading more meaningful. 🌅
Practice safety vocabulary alongside the chapter, like 'stop', 'look', and 'cross'. 🚦

funActivities.title: My Route Map Maker 🗺️
funActivities.description: Give your child paper and crayons to draw a map from their bed to the front door, or from home to school. Have them label things like 'tree' or 'shop'.

funActivities.title: I Saw It On The Way 🚌
funActivities.description: During your next trip outside, give your child a mental checklist of three things to find (e.g., a red bus, a big tree, a shop). Let them shout out when they spot them.

funActivities.title: Morning Routine Sequencing ⏰
funActivities.description: Take pictures of your child doing their morning routine (brushing, eating, wearing shoes). Print or view them on a phone and ask them to arrange the pictures in the correct order.
